HR-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
HR-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not count as a travel document.
HR-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen. A Swedish driving licence is not normally accepted as a travel document.

HR-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
HR-fakta-mobil.summary: EU roaming: the same price as in Sweden.
HR-fakta-mobil.body: You pay as at home for calls, texts and data, but the operator may set a cap on data abroad.

HR-dubrovnik-fakta-pass.title: The Dubrovnik Pass can pay off
HR-dubrovnik-fakta-pass.summary: The pass gives free admission to the city walls, museums and the city buses.
HR-dubrovnik-fakta-pass.body: The city walls, the Rector's Palace, the Franciscan Monastery museum, the Maritime Museum and the Ethnographic Museum are included in all three versions of the pass.

HR-fakta-alkohol.title: Alcohol from age 18
HR-fakta-alkohol.summary: Shops must refuse anyone who looks under 18 and has no ID.
HR-fakta-alkohol.body: The same rule applies to energy drinks. A new law also gives towns and municipalities the right to restrict shops' alcohol sales at night, so the hours may differ between places.

HR-dubrovnik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport bus to the old town in 35 minutes
HR-dubrovnik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: The bus stops at Ploče Gate and continues to Gruž.
HR-dubrovnik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: A single ticket costs 10 euros and a return 15 euros. The ticket is valid for any departure the same day. Towards the airport the bus leaves from the bus station in Gruž and stops at the cable car near the old town.

HR-split-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport bus to Split in 30 minutes
HR-split-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: The bus runs directly to the bus station by the ferry port.
HR-split-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: A single ticket costs 10 euros and a return 15 euros. From the airport the bus leaves roughly 30 minutes after each landing. In summer, traffic can make the journey longer.

HR-fakta-krka-bad.title: Swimming ban in Krka
HR-fakta-krka-bad.summary: Swimming in Krka National Park has been prohibited since 1 January 2021.
HR-fakta-krka-bad.body: Older pictures and guides show people swimming below the Skradinski buk waterfall. It is no longer allowed.

HR-zagreb-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport bus to the bus station in 35–40 minutes
HR-zagreb-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: Pleso Prijevoz runs between the airport and the central bus station.
HR-zagreb-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: The city's local buses also run from the airport but take longer.

HR-dubrovnik-stadsmuren.name: The city walls
HR-dubrovnik-stadsmuren.summary: One lap around the old town. The ticket is valid once.
HR-dubrovnik-stadsmuren.body: If you leave the walls you have to buy a new ticket. Fort Lovrijenac is included. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full lap, and go early in the day.

HR-plitvice.name: The Plitvice Lakes
HR-plitvice.summary: A national park with lakes and waterfalls. Buy your ticket online.
HR-plitvice.body: The ticket is valid for the entrance and the time you chose when buying. Save it on your phone or print it.

HR-split-diocletianus-palats.name: Diocletian's Palace
HR-split-diocletianus-palats.summary: A Roman emperor's palace that became the old town. Free and open around the clock.
HR-split-diocletianus-palats.body: A World Heritage Site since 1979, the same year as Dubrovnik's old town and Plitvice. The palace area itself costs nothing. The cellars have a ticket, sold at the desk in the palace or by the Split City Museum.

HR-split-marjan.name: Marjan
HR-split-marjan.summary: A wooded hill with the city's highest viewpoint. Free all year.
HR-split-marjan.body: The paths through the pine forest are open all year. From the summit, Telegrin, you see the old town, the islands and the mountains. You walk there from the old town or take bus 12.

HR-krka.name: Krka National Park
HR-krka.summary: The Skradinski buk waterfall. Swimming has been prohibited since 2021.
HR-krka.body: The park's own rules prohibit swimming from 1 January 2021. Expect to see the falls from the boardwalks, not from the water.

HR-zagreb-lotrscak.name: Lotrščak Tower and the noon cannon
HR-zagreb-lotrscak.summary: Every day at noon a cannon is fired from the tower.
HR-zagreb-lotrscak.body: The tower was built in 1266 to defend the city's southern gate. The cannon has fired a shot at midday since 1877. Stand on the promenade below just before twelve.

HR-zagreb-markuskyrkan.name: St Mark's Church
HR-zagreb-markuskyrkan.summary: A 13th-century church with a colourful tiled roof in the Upper Town.
HR-zagreb-markuskyrkan.body: The roof is laid like a mosaic with two coats of arms: Zagreb's and that of the Triune Kingdom of Croatia, Slavonia and Dalmatia.

HR-zagreb-brustna-relationer.name: The Museum of Broken Relationships
HR-zagreb-brustna-relationer.summary: Donated objects from loves that ended, with the story behind them.
HR-zagreb-brustna-relationer.body: The museum is in the Upper Town near St Mark's Church and is included in the Zagreb Card.

HR-zagreb-uspinjaca.name: The funicular
HR-zagreb-uspinjaca.summary: Only 66 metres long. Runs from Tomićeva Street up to Lotrščak Tower.
HR-zagreb-uspinjaca.body: The funicular links the Lower and Upper Towns.

HR-dubrovnik-ide-muren.body: Walk the full lap before the heat and the cruise passengers arrive.

HR-ide-plitvice.title: A full day at the Plitvice Lakes
HR-ide-plitvice.body: Book the entrance and time online and be there early.

HR-split-ide-palatset.title: An evening in Diocletian's Palace
HR-split-ide-palatset.body: Go in through one of the gates after dark, when the alleys are at their quietest.

HR-split-ide-marjan.title: Sunset on Marjan
HR-split-ide-marjan.body: Walk up to Telegrin with something to drink and watch the sun set over the islands.

HR-split-ide-krka.title: Day trip to Krka
HR-split-ide-krka.body: See Skradinski buk from the boardwalks. Leave your swimwear at home, swimming is banned.

HR-zagreb-ide-ovre-staden.title: The Upper Town for the cannon shot
HR-zagreb-ide-ovre-staden.body: Take the funicular up just before twelve, hear the cannon and walk on to St Mark's Church and the museum.
